title: The Promise Stands
subtitle: The Hour is not a possibility. It is an appointment.
sources: Qur'an 33:63 — 'People ask you concerning the Hour. Say, Knowledge of it is only with Allah'
Qur'an 20:15 — 'Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives'
Sahih al-Bukhari 6503 — the Prophet ﷺ held up two fingers: he was sent and the Hour is near (narrated by Sahl)
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the ten signs before the Hour (Hudhayfa ibn Asid)

chapters.heading: Almost Concealed
chapters.body: The Qur'an states the coming of the Hour as certain: 'Indeed, the Hour is coming - I almost conceal it - so that every soul may be recompensed according to that for which it strives' (20:15). Almost concealed: close enough to shape every choice, far enough that no one builds a business on the date. The Prophet ﷺ held up two fingers and said that he was sent and the Hour is near, like these two (Sahih al-Bukhari 6503) — and Sahih Muslim 2901 reports that the Hour will not come until ten signs are seen, each a catastrophe with a name. A reflection (not a report): the concealment can be read as a mercy, since a known date would change how people live. The sources give no date and this card gives none.

familyQuestion: The date is hidden but the appointment is certain. How would you spend this week if the knock came Friday?

title: The Moon Split
subtitle: The Qur'an opens Surah al-Qamar with it
sources: Qur'an 54:1-2 — 'The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two]'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3637 — the people of Makkah asked the Prophet ﷺ for a sign and he showed them the splitting of the moon (Anas)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3636 — the moon was split in two in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime, and he said 'Bear witness' (Ibn Mas'ud)

chapters.heading: And They Saw It
chapters.body: The Qur'an opens Surah Al-Qamar with it: 'The Hour has come near, and the moon has split [in two]. And if they see a miracle, they turn away and say, Passing magic' (54:1-2). Anas reports that the people of Makkah asked the Prophet ﷺ to show them a sign, and he showed them the moon split (Sahih al-Bukhari 3637); Ibn Mas'ud reports that the moon was split in two in the Prophet's ﷺ lifetime and that he said, bear witness (Sahih al-Bukhari 3636). The verse names what followed: they called it passing magic. A reflection: the verse presents the denial as refusal rather than lack of evidence.

familyQuestion: They saw the moon split and called it magic. What have you seen with your own eyes that you're explaining away?

title: The Minor Signs
subtitle: The syllabus of the centuries — read as milestones, not dates
sources: Sahih al-Bukhari 1036 — knowledge taken away, earthquakes frequent, time passing quickly, afflictions, killing, wealth overflowing (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih al-Bukhari 80 — knowledge taken away with the learned, ignorance established, wine drunk widely, open fornication (Anas)
Sahih al-Bukhari 7121 — thirty liars claiming prophethood, competition in tall buildings, wealth so abundant that no one accepts charity (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 8 — the hadith of Jibril: barefoot, destitute herders competing in tall buildings
Qur'an 81:26-27 — 'So where are you going? It is not except a reminder to the worlds'

chapters.heading: Knowledge Lifted
chapters.body: The Prophet ﷺ mapped the centuries in single sentences, and the hadith collections preserve the map: earthquakes will be frequent, time will pass quickly, afflictions will appear, killing will increase and wealth will overflow (Sahih al-Bukhari 1036); knowledge will be taken away with the death of the learned and ignorance will become established, wine will be drunk widely and open fornication will spread (Sahih al-Bukhari 80); barefoot, destitute herders will compete in constructing tall buildings (Sahih Muslim 8); about thirty liars will appear, each claiming to be Allah's messenger (Sahih al-Bukhari 7121). Each generation may read the list and see its own time in it; the sources do not tell us which signs have occurred and which have not, and this card does not decide. In Surah at-Takwir the Qur'an asks: 'So where are you going? It is not except a reminder to the worlds' (81:26-27). The signs are not given to date the Hour (7:187).

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ listed signs without dating the Hour. What do you do with a list that tells you to be ready but not when?

title: The Ten Major Signs
subtitle: The ten signs named in the hadith — the report does not fix their order
sources: Sahih Muslim 2901 — the ten signs (Hudhayfa ibn Asid): the Smoke, the Dajjal, the Beast, the sunrise from the west, the descent of Isa, Ya'juj and Ma'juj, three sinkings, and a fire driving people to their place of assembly (the report does not say that this is the order in which they occur)

chapters.heading: One After Another
chapters.body: The hadith of Hudhayfa ibn Asid says the Hour will not come until ten signs are seen (Sahih Muslim 2901). It lists them as: the Smoke; the Dajjal; the Beast; the sunrise from the west; the descent of Isa son of Maryam; Ya'juj and Ma'juj; three great sinkings of the earth — one in the east, one in the west and one in Arabia; and, last of them, a fire from the Yemen that drives people to the place of their assembly. The report does not say that the signs happen in the order it lists them, so this card does not claim one. The report has variant chains: in one the tenth sign is the descent of Isa and in another the tenth is a violent gale that drives people to the sea, and Shu'bah noted that some narrators did not trace one of those versions back to the Prophet ﷺ (Muslim 2901). The list holds the Dajjal, and it also holds the descent of Isa son of Maryam.

familyQuestion: The hadith names ten signs and gives no calendar. If the order is not given to you, what should you do about being ready today?

title: The Smoke
subtitle: A visible smoke that covers the people
sources: Qur'an 44:10-11 — 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. Covering the people; this is a painful torment'
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the Smoke among the ten signs (Hudhayfa ibn Asid)
Sahih al-Bukhari 4821 — Ibn Mas'ud's account of the smoke of the Quraysh famine

chapters.heading: A Smoke Over the People
chapters.body: 'Then watch for the Day when the sky will bring a visible smoke. Covering the people; this is a painful torment' (44:10-11). The Smoke is the first sign in the list of ten in Sahih Muslim 2901. Scholars differ on what this verse refers to. Ibn Mas'ud said it already happened: the Quraysh were struck by famine after the Prophet ﷺ prayed against them, so that a hungry man would imagine smoke between him and the sky (Bukhari 4821); the hadith of Hudhayfa counts the Smoke among the ten signs still to come (Muslim 2901). This card gives both and decides neither. Reports about how long the Smoke lasts, and its effects on believers and disbelievers, are not told here.

familyQuestion: A sign is a warning. What warning are you hearing now that you could act on before it has to be repeated louder?

title: The Beast
subtitle: A creature that speaks from the earth
sources: Qur'an 27:82 — 'We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them'
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the Beast among the ten signs (Hudhayfa ibn Asid)
Sahih Muslim 2941 — the sun from the west and the Beast in the forenoon: whichever comes first, the other follows soon after (Abdullah ibn Amr)

chapters.heading: The Earth's Witness
chapters.body: 'And when the word befalls them, We will bring forth for them a creature from the earth speaking to them, [saying] that the people were, of Our verses, not certain [in faith]' (27:82). The Beast is among the ten signs in Sahih Muslim 2901. Abdullah ibn Amr reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that the first of the signs would be the rising of the sun from the west and the appearance of the Beast before the people in the forenoon; whichever comes first, the other follows immediately (Muslim 2941). Longer reports describe what the Beast does and carries; the one commonly quoted (Tirmidhi 3187) is graded da'if by al-Albani and others, so this card leaves it out. The Qur'an's own phrasing is the lesson: it comes when the word befalls them, and it speaks.

familyQuestion: The earth will speak when the word befalls. What is the ground of your life saying about you right now?

title: The Sun Rises from the West
subtitle: The sign after which faith no longer helps one who had not believed before
sources: Qur'an 6:158 — 'no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before'
Sahih al-Bukhari 4635 — the sun rises from the west (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 2901 — the sunrise from the west among the ten signs
Qur'an 25:62 — night and day in succession

chapters.heading: When Seeing Stops Counting
chapters.body: The order of nature is the last argument: 'The Day that some of the signs of your Lord will come no soul will benefit from its faith as long as it had not believed before or had earned through its faith some good' (6:158). Abu Hurayrah reports the Prophet ﷺ saying that the Hour will not come until the sun rises from the west; when people see it, everyone on the earth will believe — and that is when, as the hadith has it, believing does a soul no good if it had not believed before (Sahih al-Bukhari 4635). The sunrise from the west is also among the ten signs of Sahih Muslim 2901. A reflection: the verse and hadith make the point that belief after this sign no longer avails one who had not believed before. 'And it is He who has made the night and the day in succession for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude' (25:62) — the alternation of night and day is itself the proof, the verse says, for whoever desires to remember or desires gratitude.

familyQuestion: The sun rises from the west only when it's too late. What are you treating as 'too subtle' that is actually your daily proof?

title: The Forty Days of the Dajjal
subtitle: Forty days that test every soul alive
sources: Sahih Muslim 2937 — the report of al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an: forty days, one like a year, one like a month, one like a week, the rest like your days
Sahih Muslim 2943 — no land the Dajjal does not enter but Makkah and Madinah, guarded by angels (Anas)
Sahih al-Bukhari 3337 — no prophet but warned his nation of the Dajjal (Ibn Umar)
Sahih Muslim 2946 — no creation causes more trouble than the Dajjal from Adam to the Hour (Hisham ibn Amir)
Sahih Muslim 809 — whoever memorises the first ten verses of Surah al-Kahf is protected from the Dajjal (Abu al-Darda)

chapters.heading: Forty Days
chapters.body: Al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an reported that the Prophet ﷺ spoke of the Dajjal, and when the Companions asked how long he would stay on the earth he said: forty days, one day like a year, one like a month, one like a week, and the rest like your days (Muslim 2937). Anas reported that there will be no land the Dajjal does not enter except Makkah and Madinah, whose passages are guarded by angels (Muslim 2943). In al-Nawwas's report he comes to a people, invites them, they believe, and the sky rains for them and the earth grows; he comes to another people who reject him, and drought comes on them and they are left with nothing (Muslim 2937). The Prophet ﷺ said that from the creation of Adam to the Last Hour there is no creation that causes more trouble than the Dajjal (Muslim 2946, from Hisham ibn Amir), and that there was no prophet who did not warn his nation of him (Bukhari 3337, from Ibn Umar). Abu al-Darda reported the Prophet ﷺ saying that whoever memorises the first ten verses of Surah al-Kahf will be protected from the Dajjal (Muslim 809; one narrator of that report said the last ten verses instead). The greatest trial came with a protection the Prophet ﷺ named in advance.

familyQuestion: The Prophet ﷺ named a protection against the Dajjal before the trial. Do you know the first ten verses of al-Kahf by heart yet?

title: The Descent of Isa
subtitle: The return the prophets promised and the Qur'an sealed
sources: Qur'an 4:157-159 — 'And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death'
Sahih al-Bukhari 2222 and Sahih Muslim 155 — the son of Maryam will descend as a just ruler (Abu Hurayrah)
Sahih Muslim 2937 — the white minaret, the gate of Ludd (al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an)
Sahih Muslim 156 — their commander invites him to lead the prayer and he declines (Jabir)
Sahih Muslim 2897 — the enemy dissolves as salt dissolves in water (Abu Hurayrah)

chapters.heading: He Descends at the White Minaret
chapters.body: Al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an's report says Allah will send Isa son of Maryam, and he will descend at the white minaret in the east of Damascus, wearing two garments lightly dyed with saffron, placing his hands on the wings of two angels; he will pursue the Dajjal and catch him at the gate of Ludd and kill him (Muslim 2937). He comes not with a new revelation but within this one: the Prophet ﷺ said he will descend as a just ruler, break the cross, kill the pig and abolish the jizyah, and wealth will become so abundant that no one will accept it (Bukhari 2222; Muslim 155). Jabir reported that their commander will invite him to lead the prayer and he will say: no, some of you are commanders over others — an honour from Allah to this ummah (Muslim 156). Another report says the enemy will dissolve at the sight of him as salt dissolves in water, and Allah will kill them by his hand (Muslim 2897). The Qur'an says: 'And there is none from the People of the Scripture but that he will surely believe in Jesus before his death. And on the Day of Resurrection he will be against them a witness' (4:159). Ibn Kathir reports that Ibn Abbas and Abu Malik understood 'before his death' as before Isa's own death, after his return, and he mentions Abu Hurayrah reciting the verse after this hadith. The report does not name the commander of the Muslims, and this card does not.

familyQuestion: Isa returns within this faith, not beyond it. What does that tell you about the Book you are holding?

title: Ya'juj and Ma'juj Released
subtitle: The wall stands by decree; the release is scheduled
sources: Qur'an 18:94-98 — the barrier, and 'when the promise of my Lord comes, He will make it level'
Qur'an 21:96-97 — 'from every elevation, descend And [when] the true promise has approached'
Sahih al-Bukhari 3346 and Sahih Muslim 2880 — 'an opening has been made in the wall of Gog and Magog like this' (Zaynab bint Jahsh)
Sahih Muslim 2937 — Allah sends Gog and Magog; they drink Lake Tiberias; Isa and the believers at Tur; the insects (al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an)

chapters.heading: Level Ground
chapters.body: 'Until when [the dam of] Gog and Magog has been opened and they, from every elevation, descend And [when] the true promise has approached; then suddenly the eyes of those who disbelieved will be staring' (21:96-97). Zaynab bint Jahsh reported that the Prophet ﷺ once came to her in a state of fear and said that an opening had been made in the wall of Gog and Magog like this, making a circle with his thumb and forefinger, and when she asked whether they would be destroyed though pious people were among them he said: yes, when the evil increase (Bukhari 3346; Muslim 2880). In al-Nawwas ibn Sam'an's report Allah sends Gog and Magog and they swarm down from every slope; the first of them drinks from Lake Tiberias and the last says there was once water here; Isa and his companions are besieged at Tur until Allah, answering their supplication, sends insects on their necks, and the next morning they are dead (Muslim 2937). A further report that they dig each day and are told 'tomorrow if Allah wills' is graded sahih by al-Albani (Tirmidhi 3153; Ibn Majah 4080) but da'if by Zubair Ali Za'i of Darussalam, so graders differ and this card does not rely on it. The Qur'an's own sentence, 'but when the promise of my Lord comes' (18:98), is what the sources agree on.

familyQuestion: The promise of Allah comes in its time. What are you postponing as if it will not?

title: The Fire
subtitle: A fire, and the gathering
sources: Sahih Muslim 2901 — the last of the ten signs: a fire from the Yemen driving people to their place of assembly
Qur'an 50:42 — 'The Day they will hear the blast [of the Horn] in truth'
Qur'an 39:68-69 — the two blasts and the earth shining with its Lord's light

chapters.heading: A Fire to the Gathering
chapters.body: The last of the ten signs in Sahih Muslim 2901 is a fire that comes out of the Yemen and drives people to the place of their assembly. This card does not try to describe anything beyond what that report says. Separately, the Qur'an describes the two blasts: 'And the Horn will be blown, and whoever is in the heavens and whoever is on the earth will fall dead except whom Allah wills' (39:68). And of the second blast: 'and at once from the graves to their Lord they will hasten' (36:51). The Qur'an goes on to describe the Day: 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth' (39:69).

familyQuestion: The sign ends and the Day begins. What would you want to be ready with on that Day?

title: The End of the Story
subtitle: The kingdom that never ends
sources: Qur'an 39:69-70 — 'and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged'
Qur'an 21:104 — 'The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records'
Qur'an 98:8 — 'Their reward with Allah will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow'

chapters.heading: Folding the Sky
chapters.body: The Qur'an describes the end of the world: 'The Day when We will fold the heaven like the folding of a [written] sheet for the records. As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We will do it' (21:104). Then the judgment: 'And the earth will shine with the light of its Lord, and the record [of deeds] will be placed, and the prophets and the witnesses will be brought, and it will be judged between them in truth, and they will not be wronged' (39:69). And then the story that outlasts the sky itself opens: 'Their reward with Allah will be gardens of perpetual residence beneath which rivers flow, wherein they will abide forever, Allah being pleased with them and they with Him. That is for whoever has feared his Lord' (98:8). A reflection: the Qur'an presents the Last Day as the end of the test and the start of the reward and judgment: 'As We began the first creation, We will repeat it. [That is] a promise binding upon Us' (21:104).

familyQuestion: The Qur'an says the promise is binding upon Allah. What are you preparing for the meeting that follows it?
